title: cross-run-history
description: The declaration of the harness-scoped logs under history_dir, and the whole of what decides which events reach them. One property per log, named for the file it declares, holding that log read as an array of parsed lines: its items.properties.event.enum enumerates the execution-history event kinds routed to that log, and its items.properties declare the fields a record there carries. Selection and record shape are therefore one file rather than a condition written into append_event, and adding a kind to a log is an edit here and nowhere else. The `event` property is the selection and is not itself projected: a record carries the other declared fields, so what routed it is read off the enum that named its kind rather than repeated on every line. A field the execution-history entry does not carry is omitted rather than written null, which is the rule execution-history.json already follows. A record is a summary and never a copy: the per-run artifacts hold the detail, and a log that duplicated them would inherit their size and lose its queryability. History is evidence, never state — nothing here is read back to make a routing decision, and the only read of a log at all is the prune that bounds it by history_retention_days. Two further logs are named here as RESERVED and are deliberately not declared above: inspection-log.jsonl and adjudication-log.jsonl. This harness has no producer for either — inspection and adjudication are level 4 concepts it does not have — so it creates neither, and naming them here rather than shipping an empty file is the whole of what it does about them. A later harness that acquires a producer declares its log as a property beside the two above, and gets the projection with no change to orchestration. The per-log declarations are properties rather than a $defs block because the harness's own validator honors a deliberately small keyword subset and refuses a schema claiming a constraint it cannot check; a property named for its log carries the same declaration and stays checkable.

execution-log.jsonl.description: One record per point an execution reached, rather than one per execution that reached an outcome. Written to .harness/history/execution-log.jsonl, one JSON object per line, appended as the point is reached rather than assembled as a terminal summary. A run that paused for capacity, was resumed and then completed therefore leaves three lines in that order, so a resumed execution is distinguishable in the record from an uninterrupted one — which is the whole reason a pause and a resume are recorded here at all: a pause carries its own exit code precisely so a caller can tell it from completion and from escalation, and an execution that reached one and left no line was indistinguishable in this log from one that never started.

event.description: The execution-history event kinds routed to this log. This enum is the selection and nothing else decides it: an entry whose kind appears here is projected into this log, and an entry whose kind appears in no log's enum is projected nowhere. The property is not projected into a record: it declares which kinds arrive here, not a field a line carries.

story_id.description: The story this execution ran, derived from the run directory's own name.

status.description: The point the execution reached, derived from the event kind that produced the record rather than threaded through the coordinator to serve this projection. Two of these values do not end an execution: capacity-paused says the run stopped to wait, and resumed says it continued, so a line carrying either is a point rather than an outcome.

retry_count.description: How many retries the execution took, counted from the retry decisions already present in the run's own execution history, which append_event has loaded to number the entry it is appending.

verifier_outcome.description: The verifier's verdict, when the entry that produced this record carried one. Absent otherwise.

timestamp.description: When the outcome occurred, in the same YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS form events.log and execution-history.json use. It is what history_retention_days is compared against.

retry-log.jsonl.description: One record per retry a story's execution took. Written to .harness/history/retry-log.jsonl, one JSON object per line, appended as the retry is routed.

event.description: The execution-history event kinds routed to this log, on the terms the execution log's own event property states: this enum is the selection, and the property is not projected into a record.

story_id.description: The story whose execution took this retry, derived from the run directory's own name.

timestamp.description: When the retry was routed, in the same YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS form events.log and execution-history.json use. It is what history_retention_days is compared against.

stage.description: The stage the entry belongs to. Absent when the entry carried none.

retry_decision.description: The routing decision the entry recorded. Absent when the entry carried none.

retry_category.description: The retry category the verifier reported, as the workflow's retry_routing table declares it. Absent on a retry that carries no category.

retry_stage.description: The stage the retry was routed to. On a self-routed entry it names the entry's own stage, because a self-route has no destination other than itself.
